title: Zhytomyr clinch 2025/26 League 1 title!
description: Zhytomyr - Chayka 100-91 Zhytomyr clinched 2025/26 League 1 title beating Chayka 100-91 in the Final game. Trailing 21-28 at the end of the first quarter, Zhytomyr replied with a 27-17 run in the second frame and produced a marvellous 34-21 third quarter to win the game. Chayka won the last stanza 25-18 but could not catch up with the winners. Vadim Dovidniy (184-G-1993) led the winners with 29 points and Oleksandr Shepelev (201-F-1994) netted 25. Igor Starodub (182-PG-1997) and Tischenko netted 18 points each in a loss.
imageCaption: Zhytomyr clinch 2025/26 League 1 title! (Photo: fbu.ua)

title: Inter SB celebrate 1 Liga title
description: FINALBlue Wings 2 - Inter SB 46-80 Inter SB dominated down low during the game scoring 44 of its points in the paint compared to Blue Wings 2's 22. They outrebounded Blue Wings 2 42-31 including 28 on the defensive glass. Inter SB brought some defensive toughness making 7 blocks. Worth to mention a great performance of the former international power forward Maros Golian (206-2007) who helped to win the game recording a double-double by scoring 28 points, 18 rebounds and 4 blocks (on 11-of-14 shooting from the field). point guard Bruno Randuska (191-2008) contributed with 12 points, 5 rebounds and 4 assists for the winners. Four Inter SB players scored in double figures. Guard Andrej Nahlik (192-2006) answered with 10 points and 6 rebounds and forward Adam Galko (205-2004) added 6 points and 6 rebounds in the effort for Blue Wings 2. The winner was already known earlier in the game, so…
imageCaption: Inter SB celebrate 1 Liga title (Photo: slovakbasket.sk)

title: Urartu Yerevan celebrate A-League title
description: Urartu - Hatis 90-94 Urartu celebrated A League title. They overcame Hatis on aggregate in the championship series despite return leg game by four points. The guests trailed by 7 points after first quarter, but they rallied back to get the 3-point lead at the halftime and eventually won the game 94-90. Hatis made 23-of-30 free shots (76.7 percent) during the game, while Urartu only scored seven points from the stripe. 25 personal fouls committed by Urartu helped opponents get some easy free throw opportunities. American forward Dannie Smith (198, college: IU Northwest) had a double-double by scoring 39 points (!!!) and 10 rebounds (was perfect 8-for-8 from the free throw line) to lead the charge for the winners and the former international forward Davit Khachatryan (210-2000) chipped in 26 points and 18 rebounds during the contest. American swingman William Henderson (211, college:…
imageCaption: ARM Urartu Yerevan celebrate A-League title (Photo: facebook.com)

title: Free UNI claim A League title
description: Free UNI - Griffin 77-57 Free UNI outgunned Griffin in the fourth game of the championship series to conquer A League trophy. The game was mostly controlled by Free UNI. Griffin managed to win third quarter 20-18. But it was not enough to take a lead and get a victory that evening. Worth to mention a great performance of American guard Kevon Voyles (190-2000, college: Marshall) who helped to win the game recording 25 points, 5 assists and 4 steals. Guard Levan Qvartskhava (194-2002) contributed with 14 points and 5 rebounds for the winners. American forward Daniel Ransom (198, college: OKBU, agency: Interperformances) replied with a double-double by scoring 21 points and 10 rebounds (made all of his eight free throws) and forward Vakhtang Gogberashvili (202-2002) added 12 points, 6 rebounds and 4 assists in the effort for Griffin. Both coaches used bench players which allowed the…
imageCaption: Free UNI claim A League title (Photo: gbf.ge)

title: Dubai Basketball Win in Belgrade to Claim a Maiden ABA League Crown
description: Dubai Basketball are the 2025/26 AdmiralBet ABA League champions, holding their nerve in a tense 83-81 road win over Partizan Mozzart Bet in Game 4 to wrap up the finals 3-1 and lift the first trophy in the club's brief history. Dubai led for most of the night but could never shake a Partizan side roared on by its home crowd, the two teams trading the lead in a contest that stayed tight across all 40 minutes. It came down to the final 15 seconds. With the score tied at 81-81, Aleksa Avramovic (193-G-1994) stepped to the line and calmly sank both free throws to put Dubai ahead 83-81. Partizan had one last chance to force overtime or win it, but the visitors' defense held: Carlik Jones (185-PG-1997, college: Louisville) was forced into a tough, contested two that missed, and Justin Anderson (198-G/F-1993, college: Virginia, agency: Octagon Europe) secured the rebound to seal the…
imageCaption: Dubai Basketball Win in Belgrade to Claim a Maiden ABA League Crown (Photo: aba-liga.com)

title: Tillman's 26 seal Sabah's fourth straight ABL crown
description: Sabah completed a clean sweep of the Azerbaijan Basketball League finals on Monday, blitzing Absheron Lions 108-95 in Game 3 at Baku Sports Hall to claim their fourth consecutive championship under legendary Lithuanian coach Rimas Kurtinaitis. American center Justin Tillman (203-F-1996, college: VCU) was named Finals MVP immediately after the clincher, capping a dominant series with 26 points on 11-of-16 from the field, eight rebounds, and two blocks. The 26-year-old attacked the rim relentlessly, converting at nearly 69 percent from two-point range as Absheron's interior defense had no answer. Hassani Gravett (188-G-1996, college: S.Carolina) orchestrated the victory with 24 points (7-of-15 from two, 3-of-6 from three), nine assists, and seven rebounds in 32 minutes, while Keith Jordan (198-SF-1998, college: SHU) added 14 points on a perfect 5-of-5 from inside the arc. James Eads III…
imageCaption: Tillman's 26 seal Sabah's fourth straight ABL crown (Photo: instagram)

title: Bamberg Baskets win the 2026 BBL Cup!
description: Bamberg Baskets have won the 2026 BBL Cup ending a seven-year title drought. In the final of the Top Four tournament in Munich, Bamberg defeated Alba Berlin 74â€“72 in a dramatic contest. It marked the clubâ€™s first trophy since their previous cup triumph in 2019. Alba controlled the boards with a 44â€“26 rebounding advantage but could not capitalize in the closing moments. Demarcus Demonia (201-G/F-1999, college: ETAMU) was named man of the match after scoring 19 points, including the decisive basket late in the game. For Berlin, Malte Delow (197-SF-2001) led the scoring with 17 points.
imageCaption: Bamberg Baskets win the 2026 BBL Cup! + stats (Photo: Bamberg)

title: Minkov's double-double earns Final Four MVP as Vidabasket complete historic Bulgarian BBL double
description: Vidabasket capped a season for the ages on Sunday, demolishing Haskovo 97-78 in the BBL National Finals title game to complete the domestic double adding the national championship to the BBL Cup they won earlier in the campaign. The Vidin-based club were utterly dominant in the biggest game of their season, never giving Haskovo a sniff as they pulled away for a comfortable 19-point victory. Final Four MVP Damyan Minkov (197-F-2002) was the driving force once again with a double-double of 24 points and 11 rebounds, continuing the form that carried Vidabasket through the entire campaign.
imageCaption: Vidabasket complete historic Bulgarian BBL title (Photo: instagram)

title: Monaco Win in Paris to Reclaim the French Title and Complete a Quadruple
description: Monaco are champions of France once again, winning a wild and dramatic Game 5 at the Adidas Arena 101-92 against Paris Basketball to take the Betclic Elite title a third crown in four years and the final piece of an unprecedented quadruple this season, achieved just before the team is broken up this summer. The decider delivered on every promise, and the drama began hours before tip-off with the announcement that Matthew Strazel (184-PG-2002) had been suspended for the game. Monaco's response was a stunner: they activated Mike James (185-PG-1990, college: Lamar), the American playmaker who had been absent since May 5 and on strike over unpaid wages at the club. Wearing the number 32 Strazel's number James did not weigh heavily on the game for long, but he was among the Monaco players who turned it around at the start of the fourth quarter. With the Roca Team seemingly buckling, trailing…
imageCaption: Monaco Win in Paris to Reclaim the French Title and Complete a Quadruple (Photo: Monaco)

title: Fyllingen rally from 2-1 down to claim BLNO title in epic five-game final against Gimle
description: Fyllingen BK are the 2025-26 BLNO champions, completing a dramatic comeback from a 1-2 series deficit to edge Gimle 80-76 in a pulsating Game 5 decider and win the best-of-five finals 3-2. The Bergen club, who topped the regular season at 23-4, had to do it the hard way against a Gimle side (22-5) that pushed them to the absolute limit across a five-game series in which all four home teams won before Fyllingen broke serve in the decider. Gimle had taken Game 1, Fyllingen leveled in Game 2, Gimle edged Game 3 to lead 2-1, and Fyllingen forced the decider with a Game 4 victory â€” setting the stage for a winner-take-all showdown.
imageCaption: Fyllingen claim BLNO title in epic five-game final against Gimle (Photo: Fyllingen)

title: Jeremy Pargo buries ten threes for 48 as Grindavik seize Icelandic crown on the road
description: Jeremy Pargo (188-PG-1986, college: Gonzaga) produced one of the most extraordinary individual performances in Icelandic basketball history on Sunday, erupting for 48 points on 10-of-16 from three-point range to power Grindavik to a 109-102 road victory over Tindastoll in Game 4 and clinch the Bonus Deildin Karla championship 3-1 before 1,653 fans. The American guard was simply unguardable. Shooting 16-of-23 from the field overall (69%), he added eight rebounds and eight assists a whisker from a triple-double for a staggering 53 efficiency in 38 minutes. When Tindastoll rallied in the fourth quarter to make a game of it with a 30-25 final period, it was Jeremy Pargo who had the answers every single time.
imageCaption: Jeremy Pargo buries ten threes for 48 as Grindavik seize Icelandic crown on the road (Photo: IG)

title: Threadgill's 29 points and Jallow's all-around brilliance clinch BOV League D1 title for Starlites in decisive Game 5
description: Starlites Naxxar captured the 2025-26 BOV League Division I championship on Sunday, pulling away from Depiro 98-77 in a decisive Game 5 at the Ta' Qali Basketball Pavilion to win the best-of-five finals 3-2 and claim the Maltese men's title. After the two sides had traded blows across four tightly contested games to reach a 2-2 deadlock, the decider was anything but tight. Starlites exploded offensively, shooting a blistering 50.8 percent from the field (32-of-63), converting 28-of-33 free throws (84.8%), and racking up 24 assists as their ball movement overwhelmed Depiro's defense in the biggest game of the season.
imageCaption: Hibernians clinch title in Game 5 decider (Photo: Hibs)

title: Kapfenberg Storm Back From 0-2 to Dethrone Oberwart for an Eighth Crown
description: Down 0-2 and staring at the end of their season, the Kapfenberg Bulls did not flinch. The Styrians reeled off three straight wins to stun the two-time defending champion Oberwart Gunners, capping the comeback with a 94-80 Game 5 victory at home to claim the win2day Basketball Superliga title the eighth championship in the club's history. It is a comeback with an echo: the only other time Kapfenberg overturned a 0-2 deficit to win a best-of-five final was in 2003, against Gmunden. As winners of the regular season and the placement round, the Bulls had entered the series as the top seed, only to drop two tight games. From there they flipped the script entirely.
imageCaption: Kapfenberg overturn series from 0-2 to 3-2 and clinch title (Photo: basketballaustria.at)

title: Biberovic's Game-Winner Seals Another Turkish Crown for Fenerbahce
description: Fenerbahce Beko are champions of Turkey once again, defending their title in the most dramatic fashion with a 77-75 win at Besiktas Gain in Game 4 to close out the Basketbol Super Ligi Finals 3-1. The decider in Istanbul came down to one unforgettable play: with the game in the balance, Wade Baldwin IV (193-PG-1996, college: Vanderbilt) conjured a pass from a near-impossible position to find Tarik Biberovic (201-SF-2001), who buried the three-pointer that won it. It was a fitting end to a tense, swinging contest in which Besiktas pushed the defending champions to the very last possession.
imageCaption: Biberovic's Game-Winner Seals Another Turkish Crown for Fenerbahce (Photo: Fenerbahce Beko)

title: Landstede Hammers Pull Away After the Break to Capture the DBL Crown
description: Landstede Hammers are champions of the Netherlands once again, overpowering Zorg en Zekerheid Leiden 90-74 at a raucous Landstede Sportcentrum to wrap up the Dutch Basketball League title. For a half, Leiden hung tough. The visitors actually edged the second quarter to keep things close, trailing by just two at the interval after a high-scoring opening in which both sides shot better than 50 percent inside. But the Hammers seized control after the break, winning the third quarter 20-14 and then blowing the game open with a dominant 24-13 final period to turn a tight contest into a comfortable 16-point triumph.
imageCaption: Landstede Hammers Pull Away After the Break to Capture the DBL Crown (Photo: IG)

title: Bosna clinch Bosnian title and double on aggregate despite OT defeat in decider
description: KK Bosna BH Telecom are the 2025-26 Bosnian basketball champions, claiming the title and a domestic double on aggregate even as they lost the deciding game 100-97 in overtime to Igokea m:tel. The Sarajevo side had built the platform for the title in the first leg, winning 76-70. That nine-point cushion proved decisive: despite falling in the return leg after an extra period, Bosna prevailed 173-170 on aggregate to seal the championship and complete the double.
imageCaption: Bosna clinch Bosnian title and double on aggregate despite OT defeat in decider (Photo: IG)

title: Hollingsworth's 28-point eruption seals back-to-back crown for Petrolina AEK
description: Petrolina AEK successfully defended their ECOMMBX Basket League championship on Monday, holding off a furious late rally from Keravnos Strovolou to win 68-64 in Game 5 of the finals at the Kition Arena and claim the title 3-2 in front of approximately 4,000 fans. Taveion Hollingsworth (188-G-1999, college: WKU) was the driving force with a game-high 28 points, including a clutch fourth-quarter performance that kept AEK ahead when Keravnos closed within a single point in the dying seconds. Jayveous McKinnis (201-F-1999, college: Ole Miss) added 16 points and Ta'Lon Cooper (193-G-1999, college: S.Carolina) had 12, including the composed free throws and a Reed Nottage (198-G, college: CBU) dunk in the closing seconds that sealed the championship for coach Christoforos Liavadiotis' side.
imageCaption: Hollingsworth's 28-point eruption seals back-to-back crown for Petrolina AEK(Photo: cbf.basketball)

title: Mastrogiannopoulos and Anderson power Vikos Falcons to historic GBL promotion with Elite League Final Four triumph
description: Vikos Falcons made history on Sunday, becoming the first team from Ioannina â€” and the first from the Epirus region â€” to earn promotion to the Stoiximan Greek Basketball League (GBL), dismantling Evertech Papagou 87-72 in the Elite League Final Four championship game at the DAK Lefkadas. Sarandis Mastrogiannopoulos (194-PG-1997, agency: Octagon Europe) was the standout performer with 21 points, three rebounds, and eight assists in a commanding display, while Quincy Anderson (193-G-1999, college: Murray St.) matched him with 21 points and eight rebounds. The pair combined for 42 points as coach Thanasis Giaples's side took control early and never looked back.
imageCaption: Vikos Falcons wins GBL promotion with Elite League Final Four triumph (Photo: basket.gr)

title: Dynasty Undisturbed: Buducnost Sweep Studentski Centar for an 18th Crown and the Double
description: There is nothing new about Buducnost lifting the Montenegrin championship, and there was nothing new about the manner of it either. The blue-and-white machine closed out the Prva A Liga final by beating Studentski Centar 94-84 on Thursday, completing a clean sweep of the title series and claiming the club's 18th national crown. It was a fitting bookend to a final that was never truly competitive on the scoreboard. Andrej Zakelj's side had crushed Studentski Centar 104-81 in the opener, and the rematch followed a familiar script. Buducnost grabbed control immediately, winning the first quarter 26-17. Studentski Centar punched back to take the second 25-21 and trimmed the gap to 47-42 by halftime, but that was as close as they would get. Buducnost re-established command after the break, edging the third quarter 23-20 to lead 70-62 and matching every Studentski Centar push in the fourth to…
imageCaption: Buducnost Sweep Studentski Centar for an 18th Crown and the Double (Photo: IG)

title: Kokila and Mokoka power JL Bourg to historic first EuroCup title with series sweep of Besiktas
description: Cosea JL Bourg-en-Bresse etched their name into European basketball history on Tuesday night, holding off a furious Besiktas GAIN Istanbul comeback to win 73-71 at Ekinox and complete a 2-0 sweep of the BKT EuroCup Finals â€” claiming the club's first-ever continental trophy and a coveted EuroLeague berth for the 2026-27 season. Kevin Kokila (204-F/C-2001) was immense in the clincher, scoring 18 points on a brutally efficient 6-of-8 from two-point range and 6-of-7 from the free-throw line while grabbing six rebounds â€” four offensive â€” and generating a game-high 27 efficiency in just over 20 minutes. Adam Mokoka (195-G/F-1998), who had been the hero of the Game 1 road victory in Istanbul, backed it up with 17 points on 6-of-12 from inside the arc, adding a game-high 10 rebounds, including four offensive boards, along with an assist and a steal.
imageCaption: Kokila and Mokoka power Bourg to historic title (Photo: Euroleague.net)

title: Peters' clutch free throws seal Olympiacos' comeback as Reds edge Real Madrid for EuroLeague crown
description: Olympiacos Piraeus are EuroLeague champions. Alec Peters (206-PF-1995, college: Valpo) sank two ice-cold free throws with 11.2 seconds remaining to put the Reds 90-85 ahead after Andres Feliz (188-PG-1997, college: Illinois)'s wide-open three-pointer to tie it rattled out, Olympiacos closed out a 92-85 victory over Real Madrid in a Championship Game that had everything a seven-point first-quarter deficit erased, a second-half seesaw, and a fourth-quarter eruption that delivered the trophy to the home crowd at Telekom Center Athens.
imageCaption: Olympiacos edge Real Madrid for EuroLeague crown (Photo: Euroleague)

title: Spartak make history: Subotica club crowned Serbian champions for the first time
description: Spartak Office Shoes are champions of Serbia for the first time in their history, edging FMP 76-73 in an overtime thriller to complete one of the most remarkable runs in the modern Serbian game a title series featuring neither Crvena Zvezda nor Partizan. The Subotica side, who had already stunned Crvena Zvezda in the semifinals, kept their nerve in a tense, see-sawing final. Spartak controlled the early going, leading 24-19 after the first quarter and pushing the advantage through a strong third (22-16) to take command. But FMP refused to fold, storming back with an 18-5 fourth quarter to force overtime at 68-68. In the extra period, Spartak outscored FMP 8-5 to seal the historic championship.
imageCaption: Spartak Subotica clinch historic first title in Serbia (Photo: KK Spartak)

title: Henkel's clutch threes and McDaniel's 21 off the bench seal Enovos League title for Etzella
description: Etzella Ettelbruck are the 2025-26 Enovos League champions, holding off a furious Sparta Bertrange rally 87-81 in Game 3 at the Centre sportif du Deich on Sunday to complete a 3-0 sweep of the best-of-five finals before 950 fans. It looked comfortable for 30 minutes. Then it looked like it was slipping away. Then Thomas Henkel (190-G-1993) buried two clutch three-pointers down the stretch that silenced Sparta's comeback and sent Ettelbruck into delirium.
imageCaption: Enovos League title for Etzella (Photo: instagram)

title: Harden-Hayes earns MVP as Sporting hold off Benfica in Mother's Day thriller to claim third Taca Hugo dos Santos
description: Sporting CP captured their third Taca Hugo dos Santos with a nerve-shredding 79-77 victory over rivals SL Benfica at the Pavilhao Multiusos de Gondomar on Sunday, composure from the free-throw line in the dying seconds securing the Leoes' second trophy of the 2025-26 season in front of 1,067 fans. The final was a fitting spectacle for a special occasion â€” played on Dia da Mae (Mother's Day), the pre-game introductions saw each player presented alongside the name of their mother in a touching tribute that set the tone for an emotional afternoon.
imageCaption: FC Porto Dethrone Benfica to End a Decade-Long Title Wait (Photo: fbp.pt)

title: Drita topple Prizreni to clinch Liga e pare title
description: Drita - Prizreni 92-91 Great defensive blocking was one of the keys in this match when Drita made 7 blocks. 25 personal fouls committed by Prizreni helped opponents get some easy free throw opportunities. The best player for the winners was Adrian Ibishi who had a double-double by scoring 18 points, 12 rebounds and 4 assists (on 7-of-8 shooting from the field). American guard Jarvis Walker (190, college: IUPUI) chipped in 20 points and 9 rebounds. Rron Dahsyla (193-2005) produced 23 points, 7 rebounds, 9 assists and 4 steals and forward Qendrim Ajazaj (193-1995) added 21 points, 10 rebounds and 4 assists respectively for the guests. Both teams had five players each who scored in double figures.
imageCaption: Drita topple Prizreni to clinch Liga e pare title (Photo: FBK)

title: Valencia Crush Barca to Win the Second Liga Title in Their History
description: Valencia Basket are champions of Spain. The Taronja produced a commanding 108-84 win at the Palau Blaugrana to close out the Liga Endesa finals 3-1 and lift the second league title in the club's history, the crowning moment of a superb season. Widely regarded as the best team in Europe over the course of the campaign, Valencia simply overwhelmed Barca with their physicality, intensity and shooting. Pedro Martinez's side took control with another irresistible display from Jean Montero (188-PG-2003), who finished with 23 points, three assists and two rebounds, superbly complemented by Kameron Taylor (198-SF-1994, college: Seton Hill) (21 points, six rebounds) and the marksmanship of Omari Moore (198-SG-2000, college: SJSU) (19 points on 4-of-6 from three). Valencia shot 53 percent from two and 48 percent from three as a team, exploiting Barca's defensive frailties and absorbing the hosts'…
imageCaption: Valencia Crush Barca to Win the Second Liga Title in Their History (Photo: Valencia)

title: Cluj Napoca celebrate Cup title
description: Oradea - Cluj Napoca 84-85 Cluj Napoca celebrated Romanian Cup title. They nipped Oradea in the Final tonight. The guests trailed by 4 points after first quarter, but they rallied back to get the 3-point lead at the halftime and eventually won the game 85-84, following a late free throw from Daron Russell. Cluj Napoca outrebounded Oradea 42-30 including a 17-5 advantage in offensive rebounds. 26 personal fouls committed by Oradea helped opponents get some easy free throw opportunities. Worth to mention a great performance of the former international point guard Daron Russell (180-1998, college: Maryland) who helped to win the game recording 21 points and 5 assists. Serbian center Dusan Miletic (213-1998) contributed with 18 points and 9 rebounds (on 7-of-9 shooting from the field) for the winners. American point guard Jaizec Lottie (188-1998, college: Flagler) answered with 25 points, 5…
imageCaption: Cluj Napoca celebrate Cup title (Photo: Cluj Napoca)

title: Reign Unbroken: Cedevita Olimpija Sweep to Sixth Straight Crown â€” on Krka's Floor
description: There was no drama left to wring out of this final, only a coronation, and Cedevita Olimpija staged it in the last place their rivals would have wanted. The Ljubljana club closed out a 3-0 sweep of Krka with an 87-71 win before 500 spectators at the Leon Stuklja Hall on Sunday, claiming a sixth consecutive Slovenian title and the 23rd of the independent era the first time in their history they have lifted the championship trophy in the heart of Novo Mesto.
imageCaption: Cedevita Olimpija Sweep to Sixth Straight Crown - on Krka's Floor (Photo: IG)

title: Randers fire past Naestved to claim Cup title
description: Randers - Naestved 101-98 (OT) Randers are 2026 Cup winners. They held off Naestved in the Final tonight. Adama Darboe (190-G-1986) came up with impressive 39 points, while X Rice added 24 points for the winners. Randers jumped off to a 32-18 lead after ten minutes. Naestved however narrowed the deficit in the second and third terms. They got within two points heading into the fourth frame 67-69. Naestved erased the deficit in the fourth quarter and finally Victor Searls (206-F, college: Ohio) gave his team an 83-81 lead with 42 seconds remaining. But Adama Darboe converted a layup to force overtime. Randers however sank 18 points in the extra period to ice the win.
imageCaption: Randers fire past Naestved to claim Cup title (Photo: Randers FB)

title: Solent Kestrels claim NBL1 Playoff title
description: Solent completed their league, cup and playoff treble with a hard-fought 74-66 victory against Worcester Wolves. In a fitting showpiece between the top-two D1M sides during the regular-season, Solent found a way to just edge ahead of a dogged opponent, as they have so many times in recent years. Drawing from across their deep roster to get themselves over the line, Solent's shared load was demonstrated by six different players contributing six or more points to the Kestrels' total, allowing the South coast programme to win their first D1M title since 2021/22. Solent's lead flirted with the 15-point mark in both the second and fourth quarter, but credit to the Wolves as they fought back on both occasions to threaten a mighty comeback. Coach Guymon's side would eventually shut the door on those plans, led by MVP Andre Arissol (188-G-1997, college: Chaminade) as he dropped a game-high 19…
imageCaption: Solent Kestrels claim NBL1 Playoff title (Photo: basketballengland.co.uk)

title: Antwerp Edge Oostende in Overtime to Seal a Historic Treble
description: Windrose Giants Antwerp are champions of Belgium for the first time, surviving a dramatic overtime in Game 5 against Filou Oostende to win the deciding game of the finals and complete a historic treble. For the first time since 2011, Belgian basketball has a new national champion. The decider lived up to its billing the first Game 5 in the Belgian finals since 2014. Threes flew at both ends early, and Antwerp were first to create separation, leading 22-28 after the opening quarter and 45-41 at the break as Oostende answered every blow. Antwerp looked to be taking control in the third, pushing the lead to ten (65-55) behind Niels De Ridder (197-F-2001), Yoeri Schoepen (200-PF-1994) and Joel Murray (183-PG-1999, college: LBSU, agency: Slash Sports), but the wildest stretch was still to come.
imageCaption: Antwerp Edge Oostende in Overtime to Seal a Historic Treble (Photo: IG)

title: Grodno-93 smother Minsk in Game 5 fight to seize ninth crown
description: There was nothing pretty about the way Grodno-93 ended their wait, and they would not have cared. In a grinding, low-scoring decider, Grodno-93 strangled Minsk 60-51 to win game 5 of the Belarusian Premier League finals and take the best-of-five series 3-2, claiming a ninth national championship at the expense of the country's most decorated club. Grodno-93 won the title where finals are usually decided on defense. They smothered Minsk into a dismal shooting night: 28.1 percent from the field overall and a near-unwatchable 1-of-19 from three-point range, just 5.3 percent. Minsk actually controlled the glass, out-rebounding Grodno-93 50-32, but never came close to converting that edge with the ball clanging off the rim all evening.
imageCaption: Grodno-93 smother Minsk in Game 5 fight to seize ninth crown (Photo: IG)

title: Sony Centre Fury Clinch SBC Playoff Title to Complete Historic Treble
description: Sony Centre Fury â€” also known as Signs Express Fury â€” have been crowned 2026 SBC Men's Playoff champions, defeating City of Edinburgh 73â€“65 in the final to complete one of the most remarkable seasons in Scottish basketball history. The victory caps an extraordinary campaign for Head Coach John Bunyan's side. Fury entered the playoffs having already secured the SBC Division 1 Championship â€” completing a stunning league "three-peat" for the second time in the club's history â€” as well as the Scottish Cup, where they edged Renfrew Rocks 71â€“68 in a dramatic final. The playoff title now completes a coveted treble: league, cup and playoff crown all in the same season. Leading the way in the final was Ali Frase, who was named MVP after a dominant performance of 25 points and 11 rebounds. Fraser's display was a fitting reward for one of Fury's most influential players, and a telling…
imageCaption: Sony Centre Fury Clinch SBC Playoff Title to Complete Historic Treble (Photo: instagram)

title: Offurum's 17 and Jurkovitz's double-double power Fribourg Olympic back to Swiss summit with 23rd title
description: Fribourg Olympic reclaimed the Swiss SB League title on Monday, dismantling Lions de Geneve 86-66 in Game 4 of the finals at the Salle Polyvalente Pommier to clinch the championship 3-1 and lift the trophy for the 23rd time in the club's storied history. After three nail-biters decided by margins of three points or fewer, the decider was anything but close. Olympic stamped their authority from the opening tip, surrendering an early 6-10 lead before seizing control with a 25-20 first quarter and never relinquishing the advantage. A 23-19 second period extended the lead to 48-39 at halftime, and a dominant 26-14 third quarter blew the game wide open at 74-53 with one period to play. The fourth quarter was a procession.
imageCaption: Fribourg Olympic back to Swiss summit with 23rd title (Photo: IG)

title: Olimpia Milano Win a 32nd Scudetto to Complete a Historic Treble
description: EA7 Emporio Armani Milano are champions of Italy once more and part of an exclusive club. Their 86-72 win over Umana Reyer Venezia in Game 4 at the Palasport Taliercio sealed the LBA Finals 3-1 and delivered a 32nd Scudetto, completing a domestic Triplete that only three other teams have ever achieved. By adding the league title to the Coppa Italia and Supercoppa Italiana they already held this season, Milano became just the fourth club in Italian history to sweep all three domestic trophies in a single campaign, after Treviso (2002-03), Siena (three times between 2008 and 2011) and Dinamo Sassari (2014-15). It was also the 18th trophy of the Giorgio Armani era, which began in 2008.
imageCaption: Olimpia Milano Win a 32nd Scudetto to Complete a Historic Treble (Photo: IG)

title: MZT Skopje Aerodrom sweep Madzari 3-0 for 13th North Macedonian title
description: MZT Skopje Aerodrom extended their stranglehold on North Macedonian basketball with a ruthless 3-0 sweep of Madzari in the MTEL Super Liga Finals, sealing a 13th championship with an 80-74 road victory in Game 3 before 500 fans at Madjari's home court on Saturday. Coach Vasko Atanasov's side trailed 26-21 after a first quarter in which Madzari's A. Hot and T. Armstrong combined for early damage. But MZT's championship composure surfaced in the second period a 25-16 burst flipped the game to 46-42 at halftime, and the visitors never relinquished the lead from there. A 16-14 third quarter and 18-18 fourth saw MZT manage the closing stretch with the poise of serial winners, converting a perfect 15-of-15 from the free-throw line across the contest.
imageCaption: MZT Skopje Aerodrom sweep Madzari 3-0 for 13th North Macedonian title (Photo: mkd.basketball)

title: Brataas' 23 guide Huddinge past Eskilstuna for Superettan crown
description: Huddinge Basket claimed the 2025-26 Superettan title on Saturday, beating Eskilstuna 73-64 in a decisive Game 3 at a packed Edbohallen before 1,048 fans to win Sweden's second-division championship and earn promotion to the SBL. Amund Brataas was the game's standout with 23 points on 9-of-17 shooting including three triples six rebounds, and four assists in nearly 40 minutes. The forward's +11 plus-minus reflected his two-way impact across a contest that Huddinge controlled from the second quarter onward.
imageCaption: Brataas' 23 guide Huddinge past Eskilstuna for Superettan crown (Photo: Instagram)

title: Ceadir-Basket Pull Away Late to Win the Moldovan Championship
description: Ceadir-Basket are the champions of Moldova. The side from Ceadir-Lunga broke open a tight contest with a dominant fourth quarter to beat Gloria 107-87 in the National Division final at the Complex Sportiv ASEM, claiming the 2025-26 national men's title. For three quarters, the final was a genuine battle. Gloria edged the first quarter 22-21 and the teams stayed locked together through the second and third, with Ceadir-Basket holding only a slender 74-71 edge entering the final period. But the champions saved their best for last, outscoring Gloria 33-16 in the fourth quarter to turn a one-possession game into a comfortable 20-point victory.
imageCaption: Ceadir-Basket Pull Away Late to Win the Moldovan Championship (Photo: moldova.basketball)

title: KK Split Crowned Croatian U17 Champions After Final Masterclass
description: ZAGREB - The Croatian U17 National Championship (Prvenstvo Hrvatske za kadete) concluded in dramatic fashion at the Dubrava sports complex in Zagreb, where KK Split put on a dominant display to defeat traditional rivals KK Cibona 88-72 in the grand finale, capturing the prestigious national youth crown. imageCaption: KK Split Crowned Croatian U17 Champions After Final Masterclass-May 25, 2026

title: Houska's 25-point, 14-rebound, 11-assist triple-double drives Valecnici Decin to U19 Boys title on home court
description: Valecnici Decin claimed the 2025-26 Czech Extraliga U19 Boys championship in front of a packed home crowd of 980, riding Marek Houska (194-PG-2009)'s sensational triple-double to an 88-79 victory over BK Sojky Pelhrimov at ARMEX Sportcentrum on Sunday. Houska was untouchable 25 points on 10-of-15 shooting (8-of-9 from two), 14 rebounds (11 defensive), and a game-high 11 assists in 36 minutes for a staggering 40 efficiency rating. The hometown star orchestrated Decin's offense with precision while dominating the glass, delivering the kind of complete performance that championship games are built on.

title: Legia Warszawa Lead Wire-to-Wire to Win the Polish U19 Title
description: Profbud Legia Warszawa are the best under-19 men's team in Poland, beating Energa Trefl 1LO Sopot 91-78 in the final of the championship tournament in Sopot. The team coached by Michal Spychala and Milosz Warecki led from start to finish, controlling the game throughout to claim the national title. WKK Wroclaw took third place, edging Exact Forestall Slask Wroclaw 72-69 in the bronze-medal game. Legia built their advantage early and never surrendered the lead, pulling away behind a balanced and efficient offense. The Warszawa side shot 50 percent from two, 38.5 percent from three and a sizzling 92 percent from the free-throw line as a team.

title: CSKA Sweep UNICS in Kazan to Seize a 13th VTB League Crown
description: CSKA Moscow finished the job in style, beating UNICS Kazan 102-76 on the road in Game 4 of the VTB United League finals to complete a clean 4-0 sweep and claim the championship. UNICS, facing elimination at 0-3, came out with the urgency the situation demanded and built an early 10-point lead, their aggressive defense producing five blocks in the opening quarter. But that physicality came at a cost: CSKA went a perfect 11-of-11 from the foul line and surged ahead in the second quarter. Despite shooting just 40.5 percent from the field to the hosts' 66.7 in the first half, the visitors leaned on a huge edge in shot volume (37-24), offensive rebounds (9-3) and forced turnovers to take a one-point lead into the break.
imageCaption: CSKA Sweep UNICS in Kazan to Seize a 13th VTB League Crown (Photo: VTB United League)

title: 2020/21 Mens National League season cancelled
description: The Basketball Ireland Men's National Competitions Committee (MNCC) has decided it has no alternative but to cancel the 2020/21 Super League and Division One league season. It follows a meeting on Saturday morning to consider the most recent Covid-19 guidelines from the Irish government. No decision has been made over the 2020/21 Men's National Cup. The MNCC is extremely disappointed that its case for commencement of play in the National Leagues on January 9th behind closed doors, with extra rigorous testing in place, has not been considered properly. It is felt that fair play and consultation has not happened and we can only conclude that we are not trusted to act in a safe and responsible manner. We note that many national basketball leagues are taking place throughout Europe with the agreement of the government and health authorities in those countries. As our clubs have commercial…

description: Nikola Kalinic (202-F-91) gave Fenerbahce a quick start. He drained two three-pointers as the hosts grabbed a 10:6 lead. Bobby Dixon then added another one for a 13:6 advantage. Fenerbahce maintained the lead throughout the first period entering the second one up by 8 points 26:18. Olympiacos started the second period strong. Ekpe Udoh (208-F/C-87, college: Baylor) soon gave Fenerbahce a double-digit advantage at 35:25. Olympiacos capped the half on a 9:4 rally to pull within five points 34:39 at halftime. title: CSKA defend VTB League title
description: Lokomotiv - CSKA 54:59 CSKA defend VTB League title as they won the fourth game against Lokomotiv. CSKA posted a 59:54 defensive win and sealed the trophy of the League again. It was another thriller in the court. The guests trailed by 6 points at the halftime before their 32-21 charge in the second half, which allowed them to win the game. Sokolov and Savrasenko were sent off the court because of the fight in the third period. CSKA Moscow dominated on the defensive end, holding Lokomotiv to just 7 points in fourth quarter. American swingman Sonny Weems (198-G/F-86, college: Arkansas) fired 24 points for the winners. Andrey Vorontsevich (207-C-87) chipped in 9 points and 9 rebounds. title: 2011 EuroLeague Final - Panathinaikos 78 Maccabi Tel Aviv 70
description: Inside a raucous Palau Sant Jordi, the 2011 EuroLeague Final tipped off with the Maccabi and Panathinaikos supporters creating a very special atmosphere as the battle commenced to finish with the Championship and become the last team standing during 2010-11. First points and first blood in the battle with Jeremy Pargo (188-PG-86, agency: Priority Sports, college: Gonzaga) went to Dimitris Diamantidis (196-G-80) with a lay-up in transition. As Panathinaikos went 4-0 in front, Guy Pnini picked up where he left off in the semi-final with a huge triple from the corner - right in front of the relieved Maccabi fans, no doubt glad to see their team get off the mark. The Greeks however made a statement inside early as they found the defence to block Schortsanitis and then for the second time in the game Ian Vougioukas went strong under the hoop to score - although he did pick up a second foul…

title: Barcelona Crowned Euroleague Kings After Routing The Reds
description: The atmosphere was fantastic at the start of the 2010 Euroleague Final Four championship game between Regal FC Barcelona and Olympiacos. The Reds were hoping to shrug off fatigue after their thrilling overtime semi-final win against Partizan while Barca were looking to deliver only a second ever Euroleague Trophy as tournament favourites. Barca went with Rubio, Navarro, N'Dong, Lorbek and Mickeal while Olympiacos put their faith from tip-off in Penn, Teodosic, Childress, Kleiza and Schortsanitis. On tip-off the entire Palais Omnisport seemed to be rocking up and down with both sets of fans bouncing on their feet and it led to great anticipation of the main event.
imageCaption: Regal FC Barcelona conquer Euroleague trophy

title: Greens are the new champions !
description: And here is the final!!! Incredible beginning by CSKA; 12-7 four minutes in the game with 6/8 shots while Panathinaikos has already made two mistakes. Vassilis Spanoulis (193-G-82, agency: Beo Basket) at 7 points from Greens' nine later (9-12). And with Pekovic and Andrew Nicholas (191-G-81, college: Maryland) at 13-12. The Greens want to hit from inside the paint and although CSKA found ways to defense initially then the whole situation changed. And the serie had not stopped; 10-0 and the score at 17-12 while the Green fans are in an ecstasy. Finally the Russians found some solutions, mainly with Holden, and the period ended at 21-16. CSKA found a lot of difficulties in the last five minutes. It should be mentioned its 0/4 3p shots. Ramunas Siskauskas (197-G-78) almost invisible, just as Smodis (no scoring).
imageCaption: Panathinaikos Athens conquer Euroleague trophy

title: CSKA captures the Euroleague Championship !!!
description: Similarly like in previous seasons, also this year Eurobasket has live coverage from the most important European clubs event - Euroleague Final Four. Final: Maccabi Tel-Aviv - CSKA Moscow 77-91 (21-22,20-20, 16-21, 20-28) Half of the arena was yellow as the Maccabi supporters were definitely the visible majority. CSKA support section was alot smaller, but they were joined by Montepaschi and Tau fans, who also cheered for the Russian team. Most of journalists predicted that CSKA would win the game as they more quality players on the paper, and at the beginning of the season not many predicted Maccabi making it to the Final Four. But after they changed the coach in the mid-season, they improved dramatically and made it all way to the Euroleague final.
imageCaption: CSKA Moscow conquer Euroleague trophy

title: After five years of drought Panathinaikos return to the top after winning an epic final
description: Panathinaikos climbed back up to the European Basketball Olympics thanks to its third win in the top continental competition, all from the hand of Serbian Zeljko Obradovic, the most successful coach in European basketball, with six Euroleague titles (or former European Cup) achieved with four different teams: Partizan (1992), Joventut (1994), Real Madrid (1995) and Panathinaikos (2000, 2002 and this 2007). The Greek team have also established themselves in Athens, their own home, despite the waste of quality, play and desire of the defending champions, CSKA Moscow, who stood up to the end, but could do nothing to stop an outstanding Greek team, touched by the muses, who made an extraordinary encounter, in particular the outer line formed by Diamantidis (MVP of the final), Chatzivrettas and Beirovic, who literally riddled the Moscow team with a devastating efficiency. It was a wonderful,…

title: Zadar beats Cibona in duble overtime winning the title
description: Game 3: Cibona vs Zadar 110-111 2OT With the best-of-three series tied at one apiece, the deciding game 3 was played on Cibona's home court, Dom Sportova, on Saturday, 26 April 1986. Supported by over 10,000 fans, despite plenty of nervy play from the home team (Drazen Petrovic (196-G-1964) getting a technical for accosting the referee and Franjo Arapovic (215-C-1965) getting ejected for striking Darko Pahlic (183-PG-1963)), Cibona had the early lead behind Danko Cvjeticanin (198-SF-1963)'s scoring (got 22 of Cibona's 42 first half points) while Drazen Petrovic, who returned to the squad after controversially sitting out game two, also scored actively. Still, Zadar kept chasing with most of its first half points coming from their twenty-six-year-old captain Veljko Petranovic (204-F/C-1959) and twenty-two-year-old center Stojan Vrankovic (217-C-1964). title: Big controversy: Bosna is a champion despite they were edged in the final game by Sibenka
description: On 9 April 1983, Sibenka and Bosna played the deciding Game 3 of their playoff final series that was decided in the last second. With Bosna up by a point and the clock winding down Sibenka had the last possession, Bosna's Sabit Hadzic was controversially adjudged by the referee Ilija Matijevic to have fouled Sibenka's Drazen Petrovic as he went up for a shot at the buzzer. Since being in the act of shooting, Petrovic got two free throws and proceeded to score both, winning the game and championship for his team. Next morning, the Basketball Federation of Yugoslavia (KSJ) presidency reviewed the game on account the time expired prior to the foul being called and on account of refereeing irregularities. They decided to void the result, ordering a single-game title playoff at a neutral venue in Novi Sad. Sibenka decided to boycott the decision. Since Sibenka refused to show up for the Novi…
